verdict.rationale: Pipecat documents Smart Turn Detection, an ML model that decides when a user has finished speaking using intonation and linguistic cues. That is first-party model-based end-of-turn detection, and STT-latency-aware turn timing adds to it. However, the evidence never explicitly contrasts it with VAD silence timeouts or shows it preventing the bot from talking over slow or pausing speakers, and the main doc sits under the Pipecat Cloud guides. missing for 10: explicit documentation of behavior on mid-utterance pauses and slow speakers versus VAD-only timeouts, configuration depth (thresholds, self-hosted use outside Cloud), independent or hands-on corroboration of turn-taking accuracy.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use model-based end-of-turn detection beyond simple VAD silence timeouts so the agent doesn't talk over slow speakers

citations.quote: Smart Turn Detection uses an advanced machine learning model to determine when a user has finished speaking and your bot should respond.
Smart Turn Detection recognizes natural conversational cues like intonation patterns and linguistic signals for more natural conversations.
Pipecat ships with measured P99 latency values for each supported service so that turn detection can account for this delay automatically.
